extraction.Name: Samuel Smith
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want his patent in fee to 317.36 acre allotment, when it was issued, September 29, 1919, but he was told that, if he did not take it, and pay his taxes, the land would be taxed just the same, and later sold for taxes, so he accepted the patent
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: in 1920, he sold his 317.36 acre allotment
extraction.Buyer: R. E. Emly, of Martin, South Dakota, for the sum of $8000.00 cash
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: he paid the year's taxes assessed against the land out of this money; did not sell his land for any debts incurred prior to receiving the patent in fee
extraction.Occupation/Income: he farms a little for a living, this being his only income
extraction.NOTES: mentally incompetent; health is poor—bad eyes, rheumatism, and feeling the effects of old age; has a wife to support, who is, also, old, feeble and rheumatic; has never received any help from the County, State nor the United States Government; considers he received a very good price for his land; document sworn March 11, 1929 | ORIGINAL_TRIBE_VALUE: "Shannon County, South Dakota (reservation not stated)" (normalized 2026-04-28 to canonical 'Pine Ridge')
